description: links (ADR 0031, ADR 0015): what a concept body's footnotes make of the map, said once for both tiers. The api derives a concept's LINKS_TO edges at every governed write (`packages/core/src/store/map/index.ts`) and the worker derives them again in the full rebuild (`apps/worker/src/better_answers_worker/links.py`); an edge's id carries its link's ordinal, so the two must count links alike or the rebuilt map and the live one name different edges. A footnote reference `[^label]` is a **citation mark** when its label, trimmed, with inner whitespace collapsed and compared without case, is the `id` of an entry in the concept's `sources` list. A mark resolves to the first entry carrying that id, whether or not the body holds a definition for it, and it is never a link: it makes no edge and takes no ordinal. A footnote reference whose label is no source id is a link when the body defines it, and it then takes an ordinal and makes an edge when its definition names a concept, as OKF allows. One with neither a source nor a definition is plain text: no edge, no ordinal, no error. A footnote definition line `[^label]: ...` is never a link and takes no ordinal. Everything else in the prose that today takes an ordinal still does. Only a record-form `sources` entry carries an `id`; a string-form entry carries none, so no mark resolves to it. Every case is read as the concept `citing` below, every target is a concept IRI no concept holds yet (so both tiers make the edge with no kind and no lookup), and no source's resource is a concept, so no case makes a lineage edge. `links` is every LINKS_TO edge the case makes, by ordinal and target, in ordinal order; `marks` is every citation mark, as written, with the index of the `sources` entry it resolves to, in body order. The TypeScript half drives the api's map write (`packages/core/test/links.contract.test.ts`) and the Python half the worker's edge derivation (`apps/worker/tests/test_links_contract.py`).

cases.case: a source-id mark is no link and shifts no ordinal
cases.body:
Claims close within 30 days.[^a] See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) for tiers.

[^a]: https://better-answers.com/c/01J6PPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPP
cases.why: The mark names a source, so even a definition that is a concept IRI makes no edge, and the ordinary link after it is the body's first link.

cases.case: a footnote defined as a concept IRI and naming no source is a link
cases.why: OKF allows a footnote to link a concept; `b` is no source's id, so the footnote stays a link and takes the first ordinal.

cases.case: a mark with no source and no definition is plain text
cases.body: Receipts are kept for six years.[^c] See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN).
cases.why: `c` names no source and the body defines nothing for it, so it is text: no edge, no ordinal, no error.

cases.case: a repeated source id resolves to its first entry
cases.why: Two entries share `a`; the mark resolves to the first of them, never the second.

cases.case: a mark matches its source id ignoring case and spacing
cases.body: Audit logs are kept for a year.[^aud-047] Reviews run yearly.[^ AUD-047 ] See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN).
cases.why: Reference labels are compared lower-cased and the customer's source ids are upper case, so a mark matches its id however its case or surrounding whitespace is written.

cases.case: a source-id mark with no definition still resolves
cases.body: Expenses over 500 pounds need a director's approval.[^a]
cases.why: A mark resolves through the `sources` list, not through a footnote definition, so a body that defines nothing for it still cites the source.

cases.case: a string-form source carries no id for a mark
cases.body: Mileage is paid at the published rate.[^AUD-047] See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN).
cases.why: A string-form entry names a resource and no id, so a mark spelling that resource resolves to nothing and is plain text.

cases.case: a footnote definition line takes no ordinal
cases.body:
Claims close within 30 days.[^a]

[^a]: The staff handbook, section 4.

See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) for tiers.
cases.why: A definition placed between paragraphs is part of its footnote, not a link, so the link after it keeps the first ordinal.

cases.case: every other link form keeps its ordinal, resolved or not
cases.body:
![a diagram](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) and [the regulator](https://example.test/regulator) back the rule.[^a] So do [nowhere], [inline](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN), [full][Price  Book], [collapsed][] and <https://better-answers.com/c/01J6PPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPP>, and so does a footnote link.[^rates]

[price book]: https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
[collapsed]: https://better-answers.com/c/01J6PPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPP
[^a]: The staff handbook.
[^ Rates ]: https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
cases.why: An image, an external link and a label the body never defines each still take an ordinal and make no edge; only the citation mark and the footnote definitions take none. A full reference's label and a definition's are compared ignoring case and spacing. A footnote's definition is found the same way, however its label is spaced or cased.

cases.case: quoted code holds no link and no mark
cases.body:
A span `[^a]` and a longer one ``[quoted](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN)`` hold nothing, and `one` and `[two](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN)` hold nothing either.

```md
[fenced](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) and [^a]
```

Only [this one](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6PPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPP) maps.[^a]
cases.why: Code spans and fenced blocks are text, so neither a link nor a mark inside one counts, however many spans of one length a line holds, and the one link outside them takes the first ordinal.

cases.case: a caret in an inline link or a reference is no mark
cases.why: Only a bare footnote reference can be a citation mark. An inline link whose text starts with a caret, and a full reference whose label does, are links like any other, even where the label names a source.

cases.case: a blank source id names no mark
cases.why: An id that is only whitespace is no id, so an empty footnote label resolves to nothing and is plain text.

cases.case: a fence opens only at the start of a line
cases.body:
Mileage is paid ~~~ at cost, see [the rates](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN).
~~~
cases.why: A run of tildes or backticks opens a fenced block only where a line starts with it, so a run mid-line leaves the link after it in the prose.
